methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: If Virginia’s ‘best state for business’ ranking falls, data center taxation debate will get the blame
signals.signal_reading: Data center taxation debate signals concentrated infrastructure investment in NoVA/select regions, reinforcing deep technical capability clustering while other regions remain excluded from the AI infrastructure layer that enables advanced deployment.

signals.title: Headlines from across the state: Spanberger weighs decisions on Oak Hill, utility refunds; more . . .
signals.signal_reading: Counties implementing data center restrictions reveal infrastructure resistance in non-metro regions, potentially blocking the physical foundation needed for distributed AI capability while metro areas advance unconstrained.

signals.title: Boeing wins $2B Space Force contract
signals.signal_reading: A $2B Space Force satellite contract to Boeing in Arlington deepens NoVA's aerospace-defense-AI integration, concentrating advanced technical expertise and defense AI applications in the metro corridor rather than distributing capability.

signals.title: Virginia legislators advance $205 billion budget including new tax on data centers
signals.signal_reading: New data center taxation in state budget acknowledges concentrated infrastructure investment but creates revenue redistribution mechanism—whether funds flow toward distributed AI workforce development or reinforce existing hubs will determine scenario trajectory.

signals.title: Amid statewide drought conditions, data centers face same restrictions as all water customers
signals.signal_reading: Drought restrictions treating data centers as standard water customers reveals infrastructure constraint friction—concentrated AI infrastructure in specific regions now competes with basic community resources, potentially limiting expansion but not distribution.
